Hi Mina,

Hope you’re well — I’m Elaine from Acme Corp. Procurement/Security. We’re running our vendor assessments for an upcoming procurement review and need Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II materials. Specific asks: 

- Formal SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) covering the audit period Jan 1, 2026 — Dec 31, 2026 (or closest available).
- If your Type II report audit period does not fully cover that window, a bridge letter describing interim controls (signed) and the exact covered dates.

- A minimal evidence manifest (high-level list of artifacts we can validate during our review).
- Preferred secure transfer options (SFTP/SharePoint/secure upload) and any whitelisting steps.

Target timeline: can you confirm availability of materials by EOD June 7? If you have a template reply or checklist we can use, that would speed review on our side.

Attached is our standard intake questionnaire (SIG-lite) — let me know if you want us to narrow the scope.

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear note and the SIG-lite. I can get this over to you; high-level options and next steps below.

1) What we can provide quickly (standard):
   - Final SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) for our most recent completed audit cycle.
   - Redwood SOC 2 coverage matrix (short mapping document).
   - Evidence manifest (high-level list; we do not provide raw logs or customer data in a package).
   - Draft bridge letter (if our audit window does not exactly match your requested period).

2) Secure transfer options:
   - SharePoint (preferred) — we’ll create a scoped folder and share link.
   - Secure SFTP — support for account creation and inbound IP whitelisting (if you need it, confirm host/IP).
   - For any signed bridge letter we can deliver a PDF via DocuSign link if you require signed copy.

3) Timing: I will coordinate with our security/compliance team. We can aim to deliver the full package or a first-pass bundle (report + coverage matrix + draft bridge letter) by June 7. If you need anything earlier for procurement gating, tell me which items are critical and I’ll prioritize.

4) Quick ask from your side: confirm the exact audit window you prefer (you listed Jan–Dec 2026) and whether Acme requires the bridge letter to be signed by our external auditor or an internal attestation is sufficient.

I’ve attached a short guidance doc (SOC2_Share_Guidance.pdf) that outlines what we typically deliver and how we redact/limit customer-identifying data.

If helpful I can set a 20-minute sync tomorrow to confirm transfer details.

Hi Elaine — quick follow-up with a proposed package and two reply templates to use internally. We’re on track to get the deliverables to you; below is what we’ll share and how.

Package we will provide (first delivery):
- SOC2_TypeII_Final_Report_2026.pdf (final auditor report) — attached in SharePoint.
- Redwood_Coverage_Matrix_2026.xlsx — short map of service -> trust criteria.
- SOC2_Share_Checklist.xlsx — manifest of artifact classes (redacted).
- Redwood_Bridge_Letter_Draft_20270530.pdf — draft bridge letter (internal-signed).

Standard transfer options (pick one):
- SharePoint link (recommended): we will provision a scoped folder and give link + expiry + download tracking. Link: https://redwood-inference.sharepoint.com/soc2/acme-intake (will send token-protected URL).
- SFTP (alternate): provide IPs and user list and we will enable inbound whitelisting.
- DocuSign (for signed bridge letter): request a sign-off flow and we’ll route to auditor/legal if needed.

What we cannot deliver: raw customer logs, decryption keys, or tenant-specific PII. Our evidence manifest lists artifact types (e.g., retention policies, sample SIEM alerts, SOC ticket snapshots) and how to request narrow scoped samples under an NDA.

Two reply templates you can paste into procurement/security workflows:

- Any IPs to whitelist for SFTP access (if you prefer SFTP).
- Whether Acme would like a 20-minute walkthrough of the package (calendar options).
